links.comparator_used: Human coder review of ten randomly selected articles, used as the reference for four LLM raters (Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek V3.2, Llama 3.3-70B, GPT-4o) applying the same source-anchored rubric
links.outcome: Agreement of LLM rater error and safety-omission detection with the human coder
links.effect: Measured error density varied about 4-fold across raters (0.150 to 0.557 errors per 100 words; Friedman p < 0.001). Of 28 sections with a source safety warning, the warning was judged missing in 22 by the strictest rater and in 4 by the most lenient. Claude Sonnet 4.6 agreed well with the human coder, while the lenient raters identified only 3 and 2 of the 9 safety omissions.
links.tradeoff: Lenient LLM raters missed most safety omissions, so the choice of rater model changed the conclusion. A rubric alone did not make a rater trustworthy.
links.quote: Cross-validation showed that the divergence was directional: Claude Sonnet 4.6 alone agreed well with the human coder, whereas the lenient raters identified only 3 and 2 of the 9 safety omissions.

design_hint: LLM-as-rater review of patient-facing summaries against source
